Taiwan is taking part in APEC China summit on an 'equal basis', president says Reuters | Updated: 12-11-2026 08:50 IST | Created: 12-11-2026 08:50 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan is participating in this year's APEC leaders' summit in China on the principle of interaction on an "equal basis", President Lai Ching-te said on Thursday, after his government called for a written guarantee from Beijing for that to happen. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation grouping is one of the few international bodies that include Taiwan, which China views as its own territory. China is this year's host, with the leaders' summit next week in the southern city of Shenzhen. However, relations between Taipei and Beijing are extremely tense. China refuses to talk to Lai, saying he is a "separatist", and its military operates around the island on a daily basis. Lai rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims. Speaking at the presidential office in Taipei to introduce computer maker Acer founder Stan Shih as his envoy to the summit, Lai said APEC is the most important multilateral mechanism for trade and economic cooperation in the region. "All members interact on an equal basis, and Taiwan is participating in this year's APEC meeting on that same principle," he added. "I want to thank the many like-minded countries that, during the preparations for the APEC meeting, have consistently emphasised the importance of Taiwan's participation in all meetings," Lai said, without naming any countries. China's foreign ministry said late Wednesday that it handles the "Taiwan region's" participation at APEC "in accordance with the one-China principle and the rules and customs of relevant APEC memorandums of understanding". "As long as these practices are followed, the Taiwan region's representatives can attend meetings as normal," it added. Lai said he wanted Shih to convey several messages at the summit, including that as the global economy faces challenges from geopolitics, energy, and supply chain restructuring, Taiwan will continue to serve as a stable and trustworthy force. "Taiwan will deepen cooperation and exchanges with key partner countries to jointly safeguard regional prosperity and stability," he added. Taiwan normally sends former officials or business executives as its APEC envoy to avoid political problems and they generally use the opportunity to speak to senior members of delegations from friendly countries like the US and Japan. US President Donald Trump is expected to have his third meeting of the year with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Taiwanese envoys have on occasion previously interacted with Xi at other APEC summits, though normally that does not go beyond a handshake or a wave. Shih was Taiwan's envoy to the 2007 APEC summit in Australia.

item.content:encoded:
FOREX-Dollar rises to 19-month high as Fed hike bets grow, yen softens Reuters | Updated: 12-11-2026 08:41 IST | Created: 12-11-2026 08:41 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The dollar climbed to a 19-month high against major peers on Thursday, supported by growing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, while the yen edged toward the key 160-per-dollar level following a dovish central banker's speech. Traders ramped up bets on further Fed tightening after stronger-than-expected October inflation data and a series of hawkish remarks from US central bank officials, who expressed concern over stubborn inflation and left open the possibility of a larger 50-basis-point increase. Some major brokerages, including Goldman Sachs, now expect another hike early next year, in addition to one in December. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose by 0.15% to 103.02, the highest since April 2025. New York Fed President John Williams is set to appear on a panel late Thursday that will be closely watched given his "pre-October FOMC meeting views the Fed had time on rate hikes," said Gavin Friend, senior markets strategist at National Australia Bank, in a note. "Fast forward two weeks and following a hotter-than-forecast October CPI report, Fed officials appear to be falling over themselves to talk up rate hikes," Friend said. "Any guidance from Williams will be seized on." Against the Japanese yen, the dollar reversed an earlier decline to trade 0.04% higher at 159.83, underpinned by wide interest-rate differentials as traders increased bets on further Fed hikes. It hit a more than two-month high earlier on Thursday. Bank of Japan board member Toichiro Asada, one of two dovish policymakers who dissented from September's decision to increase borrowing costs to 1.25%, pushed back against calls within the board for a near-term interest rate hike, saying in a speech that premature rate hikes could hurt growth and push down underlying inflation. Earlier a warning from Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura that it was "too early to forget" intervention by Japanese authorities during the summer pushed the dollar/yen pair to its lowest point of the day but the respite for the yen was brief. "Once dollar/yen rises above 160, I think caution will increase another notch," said Sho Suzuki, market analyst at Matsui Securities. "For it to move higher from there, the dollar would need to strengthen further, for example, through a further rise in expectations for Fed rate hikes, or a drop-off in expectations for BOJ rate hikes. Without something like that, the pair may lack enough momentum to test a break above 160," he said. Many analysts in a Reuters poll expect the next BOJ rate hike as soon as next month. That view was strengthened on Thursday by data that showed Japan's annual wholesale inflation re-accelerated to 7.1% in the year to October, up from a 6.8% annual increase in September. The euro was up 0.06% against the US dollar at $1.1096 while sterling slipped 0.1% to $1.3266. The Australian dollar was little changed versus the greenback at $0.6847, while New Zealand's kiwi was down 0.05% at $0.5559. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.63% to $73,848.24. Ether declined 0.49% to $2,058.18.

item.content:encoded:
Tennis-Tunisian Jabeur targeting WTA Tour return in 2027 Reuters | Updated: 12-11-2026 08:40 IST | Created: 12-11-2026 08:40 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former world number two Ons Jabeur said she hopes to return to professional tennis in 2027, after the Tunisian gave birth to her first child in April. Jabeur took a break from tennis last year following her first-round exit at Wimbledon, citing injuries and fatigue. She later extended her break after announcing she was pregnant. "I'm hoping to come back, hopefully next year. I still don't know the exact time, but very soon," the three-times Grand Slam runner-up told The National in an interview published on Wednesday. "I'm still discovering ... my body is a bit changed after the delivery, but I'm definitely coming back and hoping to stay a few more years on tour before actually retiring. "I'm enjoying everything with my son. He actually comes with me when I train. I'm trying to come back slowly." The 32-year-old, dubbed by fans as the "Minister of Happiness" for her cheerful personality, has won five WTA titles and became the first Arab woman to reach a Grand Slam final in 2022, finishing runner-up at Wimbledon to Elena Rybakina.

item.content:encoded:
US says China agreed importance of leader-level talks to advance denuclearization Reuters | Updated: 12-11-2026 08:23 IST | Created: 12-11-2026 08:23 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi agreed on Wednesday on the importance of leader-level talks to advance peace and denuclearization, including in any trilateral summit with Russia, the US State Department said. Rubio spoke in a call with Wang Yi to discuss US President Donald Trump's travel to the APEC summit in China next week and Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Florida to attend next month's G20 summit, the State Department said in a post on X. It said the two recalled the leaders' "commitment to a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity." The leaders "agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization, including at any potential trilateral leaders meeting with Russia," it added. China's earlier readout of the call between Rubio and Wang made no mention of talks on denuclearization or a trilateral summit with Russia. Xi and Trump have met twice already this year and Rubio told reporters on Tuesday there was work underway to arrange a trilateral meeting on the APEC sidelines involving Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said on Sunday he thought he would meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen to discuss ending the war in Iran and denuclearization. He said in October he was open to three-way arms control talks with Xi and Putin, which he said would focus on nuclear weapons, although China has appeared less keen on such discussions. China's Foreign Ministry said last month that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage." China's state news agency Xinhua said Wang held a "positive and constructive" call with Rubio, with Beijing expressing willingness to strengthen communication and cooperation with Washington. According to Xinhua, Wang said the current stability in China-US relations had not come easily and called it "a rational choice made by the two major countries based on respective and shared interests." The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin has pitched using a trilateral meeting to discuss an end to Russia's long-running war in Ukraine. This year's Trump-Xi summits appear to have helped stabilize relations, but have done little to narrow the broad differences between the two strategic rivals. In Washington in September, they agreed a two-month extension of a trade truce that had been due to expire in November, but disputes over tariffs, Chinese purchases of US goods, rare earth exports and technology restrictions remained unresolved. On Tuesday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides would advance a new dialogue on artificial intelligence, but should harbor no illusions about their differences as they seek to manage the technology's risks while competing for AI supremacy.
